_doc: Shared vectors of the cost table (specs/20261115-crm-offer-wizard T4, rules C1-C9, DD-34/35/39): run by crm-api and its crm-ui copy. Each case = CostRowIn[] -> CostResult. Cases of the same group must agree on oneOffCents and yearlyCents (placement invariance, AC-4.6).

percentage, one total row: 1000.00 + 500.00 - 10% = 1350.00 (the legacy 018 result)
percentage, no total row: the same figures
percentage, total row before the discount: the base is still the whole table
percentage rounds half up once: 10% of 25 cents is 3
percentage rounds down below the half: 10% of 24 cents is 2
percentage rounds half up: 10% of 35 cents is 4
percentage of the largest base keeps every digit (BigInt)
percentage base is one-off only: a yearly line is not in it
percentage with two total rows is refused (template line)
percentage with two total rows is refused (extra line)
every percentage is refused with three total rows, one error each, in row order
an amount discount with two total rows is valid

C4: a percentage with no one-off line has no base
C5 alone: a discount larger than its span but not than the document's one-off lines
C6 alone: yearly lines do not count towards what a discount may take (the legacy rule)

C6 names the LAST discount
a discount equal to its span is valid and prints 0
an amount discount multiplies unit by quantity
an empty span prints no figure and is not an error
a total row first: the empty span before it
an option line alone in a span makes it empty
a counted line with no unit: the span is incomplete and its checks wait
a counted line with no quantity is incomplete too
a discount with no amount: its span is incomplete
an incomplete span does not stop the next one
a percentage over an incomplete base waits
an option line after the last total: numbered, priced, counted nowhere
discounts are unnumbered; the option follows the counted lines
an option line with no price waits for nothing
an option line is not the base of a percentage
no counted line: only an option
no counted line: no row at all
ten lines counting the option are allowed
eleven lines (option included) are too many
an extra line counts too: ten template lines plus one extra
too many lines do not stop the arithmetic or hide another error
unit x quantity exactly at the limit is valid
unit x quantity above the limit: too large, the line is incomplete
a huge product beyond 2^53 is refused, not rounded
two lines at the limit add up exactly
unit times quantity
